El método lo publicó Legendre en 1805 y: The method was published by Legendre in 1805 and claimed by Gauss, who had used it to find the dwarf planet Ceres. The word regression is Francis Galton's, who in the 1880s compared the heights of parents and children and saw that the children of very tall parents tended to be somewhat less tall than them: they “regressed towards the mean”. Galton read it as a law of heredity; in reality it is a statistical effect that appears whenever two measurements are not perfectly related.

Se miden tres puntos que deberían estar: Three points are measured that ought to lie on a line, and they do not: every measurement has error. The line $y = c_0 + c_1 t$ would have to satisfy three equations with only two unknowns, and such a system almost never has a solution. In [[pe-bidimensional]] it was solved with the regression line and a formula you had to take on trust. This topic explains where it comes from: it is a projection, the same idea as the shadow of a vector in the [[ge-vectores|dot product]], carried into spaces of more dimensions. You need the dot product, the transpose and the inverse of a matrix.

Si $A$ tiene inversa, el sistema tiene s: If $A$ has an inverse, the system has an exact solution and the least-squares one is that very solution: the parabola passes through all three points.
Si hay tantas medidas como coeficientes: If there are as many measurements as coefficients —three points for a parabola—, the system has an exact solution, the residual is zero and the fit passes through every point. With more measurements than coefficients, the fit averages the errors out. And with too many coefficients for too few measurements, the model fits the data so well that it starts fitting the noise too: that is overfitting, the great danger of machine learning.
